name: MonarchEscalationPolicyEditor
title: EscalationPolicyEditor
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchCard levels, each with MonarchDurationInput (TextField with a Stepper) for the delay and MonarchCheckboxGroup (Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox)) for the targets
summary: Edits an escalation ladder: at each level, after how long and whom to notify, so an alert or request nobody acts on reaches someone else.
whenToUse: In incident, on-call or support settings, where an admin sets who is told when nobody acknowledges.
whenNotToUse: For ordered approvers use MonarchApprovalChainEditor. For one response-time target use MonarchSlaIndicator to show it and a MonarchDurationInput to set it.
api: init(levels: Binding<[MonarchEscalationLevel]>, targets: [MonarchEscalationTarget], timing: MonarchEscalationPolicyTiming = .cumulative, description: String? = nil, defaultStepMinutes: Int = 15, minLevels: Int = 1, maxLevels: Int = 10, showsErrors: Bool = false, labels: MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels = MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels(), makeID: @escaping @MainActor () -> String = { UUID().uuidString })
nonisolated static func validate(_ levels: [MonarchEscalationLevel], timing: MonarchEscalationPolicyTiming = .cumulative) -> [String: MonarchEscalationLevelProblem]
MonarchEscalationTarget.init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil)

options.name: levels
options.description: The levels in order: id, minutes before the level fires, and the ids of the targets it notifies.

options.name: targets
options.description: What a level can notify: channels, people, rotas.

options.name: timing
options.description: cumulative: times count from the start and must increase. interval: each time counts from the previous level.

options.name: defaultStepMinutes
options.description: Minutes added to the last level for a new one.

options.name: minLevels
options.description: The fewest levels; remove is disabled at this count.

options.name: maxLevels
options.description: The most levels; the add button becomes "A policy can have up to 10 levels.".

options.name: showsErrors
options.description: Shows each level's problem, for example after a save attempt.

options.name: makeID
options.description: Makes the id of a new level.

states.name: levels
states.description: One card per level: "Level 1", the summary, Remove, After (a duration with a stepper) and Notify (checkboxes).

states.name: no targets
states.description: A warning with an icon: there is nothing to notify yet.

states.name: missing targets
states.description: With showsErrors, the checkbox group shows "Choose at least one target …".

states.name: out of order
states.description: With showsErrors and cumulative timing, the delay shows "This level must come later than the one before it.".

states.name: full
states.description: The add button is replaced by a muted note.

appearance: Monarch cards on the surface colour with a label-weight title, a muted summary, the Monarch duration field and checkboxes; the no-targets warning uses the strong warning role and problems the strong danger role, each with an icon. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web shows a numbered marker beside each level and an ordered list; iOS shows the number in the title and reads each level as one container. The web uses Checkbox and DurationInput; iOS uses MonarchCheckboxGroup and MonarchDurationInput, whose stepper replaces the web's arrow keys. Levels are not reordered, as on the web: their order is the order of their delays. The web moves focus after add and remove; iOS leaves focus to VoiceOver. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The list is a container named "Escalation levels".
Each level is a container read as "Level 1, After 1 hour, 30 minutes, notify On-call rota", with the delay spelled out in the locale; the visible short summary is hidden to avoid reading it twice.
The remove button is named "Remove level 1" and is disabled at minLevels.
The delay and the targets are labelled fields; problems are text with an icon on the field they concern.
The no-targets warning is text with an icon, not only colour.
Touch targets are at least 44 points.
edgeCases: A delay cleared in the field becomes one minute.
Target ids that are no longer offered are read by their id in the summary and dropped when a box is changed.
Interval timing never reports order problems.
Long target names wrap in the checkbox group and the summary.

examples.template:
MonarchEscalationPolicyEditor(
    levels: $levels,
    targets: [
        MonarchEscalationTarget(id: {{targets.0.value}}, label: {{targets.0.label}}),
        MonarchEscalationTarget(id: {{targets.1.value}}, label: {{targets.1.label}}, description: {{targets.1.description}}),
        MonarchEscalationTarget(id: {{targets.2.value}}, label: {{targets.2.label}}, description: {{targets.2.description}}),
        MonarchEscalationTarget(id: {{targets.3.value}}, label: {{targets.3.label}}, description: {{targets.3.description}}),
    ],
    description: {{description}},
    showsErrors: true,
    makeID: { "level-\(levels.count + 1)" }
)
examples.code:
MonarchEscalationPolicyEditor(
    levels: $levels,
    targets: [
        MonarchEscalationTarget(id: "oncall", label: "On-call rota"),
        MonarchEscalationTarget(id: "chat", label: "Team chat", description: "Chat channel"),
        MonarchEscalationTarget(id: "email", label: "Operations email", description: "Email list"),
        MonarchEscalationTarget(id: "lead", label: "Team lead", description: "Person"),
    ],
    description: "Each level fires only if nobody has acknowledged yet. Times are measured from when the incident opened.",
    showsErrors: true,
    makeID: { "level-\(levels.count + 1)" }
)
